responseText:
I can’t generate a bitmap image here because no image-generation tool is available. I won’t pretend an image was created. I can, however, give you:

- ready-to-run text prompts (for when you have an image generator),
- a precise color/composition spec,
- and a step-by-step watercolor painting guide so you (or an illustrator) can produce a square watercolor lighthouse-in-fog.

Pick which you want first, or I can provide all three — below I include all.

1) Ready-to-run prompts (square output)
- For general use / Stable Diffusion / DALL·E:
  "Square watercolor painting of a solitary lighthouse standing on a rocky promontory, heavy fog rolling in, soft, diffuse morning light, delicate wet-on-wet washes, subtle granulation, muted cool palette (soft blues, gray-greens, warm off-white for lighthouse), minimal high-contrast details, loose brushwork, paper texture visible, atmospheric depth, calm sea, gentle reflection. 1:1 aspect ratio, high detail, painterly, authentic watercolor look, soft edges, no text."

- Midjourney-style (concise tokens):
  "Square watercolor lighthouse in fog :: watercolor texture :: wet-on-wet soft edges :: muted palette :: cinematic fog :: 1:1 --v 5 --ar 1:1 --stylize 250 --quality 2 --no text,photorealism,sharp digital artifacts"

- Suggested negatives/avoidances (use as negative prompt):
  "no text, no logos, no photorealistic rendering, no high saturation, no hard edges, no people, no modern buildings, no digital artifacts"

- Suggested output/resolution:
  2048 x 2048 px (or 3000 x 3000 px for print). If generator accepts seeds, pick one for reproducibility.

2) Color palette and composition (exact guidance)
- Square canvas: use rule of thirds — place lighthouse slightly off-center (upper-right or upper-left third).
- Palette (hex references):
  - Fog wash: #E6EEF3 (very light cool gray-blue)
  - Distant sky: #C7D6DE (muted blue-gray)
  - Sea midtones: #8DA3AD (desaturated teal)
  - Rocks/dark accents: #556568 (muted slate)
  - Lighthouse body: #F6F3EE (warm off-white)
  - Lighthouse roof/trim: #8A4940 (muted brick)
  - Deep shadow accents: #3B4A4F
- Tone: keep mid-to-low contrast; fog mutes contrast toward background; strongest edges only on nearest rocks and small elements of the lighthouse (light beam can be barely visible).
- Paper texture: cold-pressed watercolor paper visible; use granulating pigments or add light paper grain overlay in digital generation.

3) Step-by-step watercolor painting guide (square, ~8–12 in)
Materials:
- Cold-pressed watercolor paper (300gsm), square (e.g., 10 x 10 in).
- Round brushes: large (size 10–14), medium (6–8), small detail (2–4).
- Masking fluid (optional), metal ruler for horizon if needed.
- Palette: ultramarine or phthalo blue, payne’s gray, sap green or neutral green, burnt sienna, titanium white gouache (optional for highlights), warm off-white mix.

Steps:
1. Light pencil sketch: block in the horizon low (lower third), sketch lighthouse simple vertical shape on a promontory. Keep lines minimal—this is a watercolor study.
2. Apply clean water to sky/fog area with a large brush (wet-on-wet). While wet, drop in a pale wash of diluted ultramarine + a touch of neutral gray (#E6EEF3 area). Let it blend softly.
3. While still damp, lift tiny areas with a clean brush to suggest fog density variations. Avoid hard edges.
4. Paint distant sea: wet-on-wet horizontal strokes of muted teal (#8DA3AD) blended into the fog wash. Keep values light and soft.
5. Rocks and promontory: using a mix of burnt sienna + payne’s gray + a touch of ultramarine, use a medium brush to block in dark shapes near the lighthouse. Use dry-brush texture in places for rock grain. Keep edges slightly softened towards the fog.
6. Lighthouse base coat: dilute warm off-white for the body, let it settle slightly into the wet background so edges are soft. Reserve slightly crisper edges on the near side by letting that area dry a little more first.
7. Add architectural accents (roof, windows) with a small brush and muted brick #8A4940 and dark slate for shadow. Keep details minimal — suggest rather than define.
8. Fog/atmosphere: glaze very thin washes of cool gray over parts of the scene to unify and lower contrast. Use a soft sponge or a dry wipe to lift more fog where needed.
9. Light beam (optional): with very diluted warm-off-white or very pale gray, paint a faint triangular sweep; soften edges immediately with a damp brush to blend into fog.
10. Final accents: add the darkest accents sparingly (deep rock crevices, top of lighthouse lantern room) to anchor the composition. If desired, a touch of titanium-white gouache for a tiny highlight on the lighthouse edge.
11. Let dry flat. If you used masking fluid, remove it only after fully dry and touch up any revealed whites.

Techniques/tips:
- Wet-on-wet produces the soft foggy gradients; reserve wet-on-dry for sharper nearest-edge detail.
- Work light to dark.
- Resist overworking; foggy scenes benefit from restraint.
- For stronger texture, sprinkle a bit of table salt into damp washes on rocks/sea then brush off when dry.

4) If you want a printable digital watercolor effect
- I can produce a detailed layered SVG-like stylized vector description or CSS-reproducible mockup (not true watercolor raster), but that will not be a genuine watercolor bitmap. Tell me if you want that.

Which would you like next: a tuned prompt for a specific generator (name the generator), a printable high-res prompt + negative prompt file text, or a more detailed in-person painting plan (paper size, pigments, and timing)?
